Access control enforcement flow (rule → context → orchestrator → store)
Data-driven renderers implementing the skeleton contract

nodes.label: Config-driven engine (createPortalApp)
nodes.rationale: Screens are described as plain Route/Configuration/LayoutElement objects; the engine matches the URL, assembles a render tree, resolves dependencies, and renders — so pages are almost never hand-written.

nodes.label: usePortalRouter (route-id navigation)
nodes.rationale: Components navigate by route id, never next/navigation or next/link directly, so URL structure stays a config concern.

nodes.label: Better Auth session architecture
nodes.rationale: Server-side sessions (DB rows), not JWTs — every check is a lookup so revoking a session is a delete. The web app proxies /api/auth/* to the API so the session cookie stays same-origin.

nodes.label: Route guards (authenticationGuard)
nodes.rationale: The SDK stays auth-agnostic: routes declare guard types, the app supplies guard functions via createPortalApp, run server-side before any data fetch.

nodes.label: HirePilotX theme-only design system
nodes.rationale: MUI theme overrides + variants only, no wrapper components; one action colour (navy), amber secondary marks the one thing in motion; cards separate with shadow never border. Missing looks become theme variants, never inline chrome.

nodes.label: API layering (route → controller → service → model)
nodes.rationale: Routes are wiring only (auto-registered via Bun.Glob), controllers shape HTTP, services are HTTP-free business logic, models are schema only.

nodes.label: TypeScript 7 + Next 16 build gotcha
nodes.rationale: TS7 native port lacks the compiler API Next needs, so every Next app sets typescript.ignoreBuildErrors + experimental.useTypeScriptCli; types are gated by tsc --noEmit (both turbo typecheck for apps AND root tsc for packages).

nodes.label: Separate distDir for dev vs build
nodes.rationale: next dev uses .next-dev, next build uses .next — sharing one directory caused ChunkLoadError when a build overwrote chunks a running dev server was serving.
nodes.norm_label: separate distdir for dev vs build

nodes.label: Autocomplete renderInput input-slot gotcha
nodes.rationale: Overriding the input slot inside renderInput drops the ref MUI threads through params, making every dropdown render empty; regressed three times, now guarded by check:autocomplete.

nodes.label: Unknown IconRenderer name renders nothing
nodes.rationale: ICON_REGISTRY[name] miss returns null, so a typo is a silently blank cell; check:icons fails the build on unknown names.

nodes.label: react-apexcharts blank under React 19 + Turbopack
nodes.rationale: The wrapper renders a blank canvas, so the shared Chart drives core apexcharts imperatively (dynamic import, recreate on change); never pass undefined-valued top-level option keys.

nodes.label: Feature component 5-file pattern
nodes.rationale: component/configuration/translations/datasource/bootstrap split keeps structure, text, and data access declarative and separately swappable; the .component.tsx is skipped entirely when it would only forward to a shared renderer.

nodes.label: Binding shared renderers directly as ComponentDefinition.value
nodes.rationale: The engine injects id/configuration/data/translation, and renderers read their slice by id — so a table/stat/funnel screen needs no wrapper component, just config + datasource.
nodes.norm_label: binding shared renderers directly as componentdefinition.value

nodes.label: Injected id = component id, not element id
nodes.rationale: The engine keys configurationMap/dataMap/translationMap by element.componentType because those all come from the ComponentDefinition; naming the element id in a translating config silently falls back to raw keys.
nodes.norm_label: injected id = component id, not element id

nodes.label: data={} footgun (seedRows / seedRecord)
nodes.rationale: The engine injects data={} when there is no prefetch and useFetch skips fetching for any non-undefined data, so renderers must normalise via seedRows/seedRecord from @recruit/shared or they silently render empty — how GraphRenderer shipped blank.

nodes.label: Composition rules (atoms → shared → features)
nodes.rationale: Themed MUI atoms build shared components; shared renderers build feature modules driven by *.configuration.ts; rendering logic is never reimplemented in a module.

nodes.label: Access control (access rules on config objects)
nodes.rationale: UI filtering is cosmetic — denied routes redirect, denied elements/config parts are silently stripped; the API enforces for real.
nodes.norm_label: access control (access rules on config objects)

nodes.label: FormWithSectionsRenderer (sectioned page forms)
nodes.rationale: One form (single useForm + ajv) rendered as titled Card sections; preferred over hand-placed Fields for any multi-card settings/profile screen. Two-column layouts are section groups with grid sizes — pure config, no hardcoded columns.

nodes.label: Form widget system (schema-driven widgets + inference)
nodes.rationale: Widget resolution: explicit widget key, else inferred from schema shape (array+enum → checkbox-group, enum → select, boolean → switch, format password/date, else text). All text values are translation keys.

nodes.label: Custom widgets escape hatch (widgets prop)
nodes.rationale: The widget name IS the key, resolved from the widgets prop before built-ins. Called as a plain function, not mounted as a component — so an inline arrow is safe (component identity would remount and drop focus), but it shares the enclosing hook order so keys must not swap conditionally.

nodes.label: Validation & normalization split
nodes.rationale: The resolver strips empty strings before ajv so required fails on blanks and optional blanks skip format checks. Cross-field rules ajv can't express go in onSubmit; authoritative normalization (trim, E.164, URL canonicalization) belongs in the backend service.

nodes.label: GenericRenderer (value/cell dispatcher)
nodes.rationale: One value vocabulary (entity, pill, status, ai-match, score-bar, date, …) shared by tables, cards, lists and stat cards; a repeated look becomes a new type here, never bespoke markup in a feature.

nodes.label: IconRenderer + ICON_REGISTRY
nodes.rationale: The ONLY icon source — features never import @mui/icons-material. Must forward className or MUI slot APIs (Chip icon, ListItemIcon) silently lose their styling hook.

nodes.label: LinkRenderer (the only navigation primitive)
nodes.rationale: Resolves route ids to SPA links; can wrap any component as children. queryParams can carry serialized filters/sort so a link pre-filters the target screen.

nodes.label: CardRenderer (one renderer for every feature card)
nodes.rationale: A new card is a config, not a file. Never nest a link inside a linked card — <a> in <a> throws a hydration error; the footer auto-drops action links when a top-level link is set.
nodes.norm_label: cardrenderer (one renderer for every feature card)

nodes.label: StatCardRenderer
nodes.rationale: Grid columns come from each card's span in config, never a prop — there is deliberately no gridTemplateColumns prop.

nodes.label: MessageAlertRenderer (inline insight/warning strips)
nodes.rationale: showPath gates the strip on a data path being non-zero so a data-driven alert disappears when its condition clears — always set it.

nodes.label: BarChartRenderer (CSS design-match chart)
nodes.rationale: Built as CSS/flex, not chart-library output, because the design's chrome (peak badge, conversion pills, inset highlight) is beyond what ApexCharts can draw.

nodes.label: StageFunnelRenderer (pipeline health board)
nodes.rationale: Insight note reads from the fetch's meta ({ bottleneckStage, bottleneckCount }) so the whole card is one request.

nodes.label: GraphRenderer (ApexCharts config-driven graphs)
nodes.rationale: categoryLabelPrefix keeps axis labels in translations (API returns keys); categoryType datetime means the API returns raw YYYY-MM-DD, never display text.

nodes.label: SlidingPillTabs (sliding gradient pill)
nodes.rationale: The app's one pill tab bar — an absolutely-positioned pill measured against the active tab so switching slides instead of swapping backgrounds; every new segmented control goes through it.

nodes.label: useLocale preference store (server-seeded)
nodes.rationale: Seeded server-side on boot (getBootLocale fetches effective prefs) so first paint is correct on any device; localStorage is only the fallback when the server gave nothing.

nodes.label: Every data-driven renderer owns a skeleton
nodes.rationale: Each renderer renders a placeholder from useFetch isLoading that mirrors its real geometry so nothing resizes when data lands.
nodes.norm_label: every data-driven renderer owns a skeleton

nodes.label: AccessRule ({ resource, action?, attributes? })
nodes.rationale: action defaults to ["read"]; attributes add ABAC on top of RBAC; "*" resource is the admin wildcard. Actions are not limited to CRUD once declared in the unions.

nodes.label: Server-side access enforcement pipeline (orchestrator)
nodes.rationale: accessResolver → canAccessRoutes (redirect on deny) → filterConfigurationsAccess (drop elements) → filterConfigAccess (deep-walk configs). Components receive a configuration already scoped to the user, so feature components never write access checks.

nodes.label: role_permission store (per-agency Postgres rows)
nodes.rationale: One jsonb resource→actions row per (agency, role); the DB is the runtime source of truth. listPermissions only seeds when an agency has zero rows, so new resource keys need a migration/backfill for existing agencies. updateRolePermissions replaces the whole map — unrendered resources get wiped on save.

nodes.label: Never branch on a role name
nodes.rationale: Built-in roles are just predefined permission sets — checking a permission instead of a role name is what allows custom roles later without code changes.
nodes.norm_label: never branch on a role name

nodes.label: Permissions are not monotonic by seniority
nodes.rationale: submissions.approve is client-only; the Owner does not hold it. Never derive one role's set from another's or assume higher ⊇ lower.
nodes.norm_label: permissions are not monotonic by seniority

nodes.label: Typo'd resource silently hides UI
nodes.rationale: canAccess denies any resource absent from the user's map and the element is stripped without warning; there is no unknown-resource check, so grep the union before inventing a name.

nodes.label: Target capability matrix
nodes.rationale: Optional cells are agency-configurable and default off; View/Limited/Connect-own are scoped variants, not separate keys.

nodes.label: Dotted permission keys (domain.action)
nodes.rationale: domain.action is the authoring form of the existing AccessRule (members.invite = { resource: "members", action: ["invite"] }); canAccess does set-membership on action strings, so adopting the vocabulary means widening unions, not rewriting the engine.

nodes.label: Client isolation as a hard query-scope boundary
nodes.rationale: A client must never see other clients, recruiters, billing, internal notes or audit logs — enforced as a query-level scope in the service layer, not a UI permission toggle, because a canAccess rule only hides UI and leaks through direct API calls.
nodes.norm_label: client isolation as a hard query-scope boundary

nodes.label: Workspace vs account settings split
nodes.rationale: Workspace defines defaults, account may override; account settings are personal and never permission-gated. Report accent and UI accent are kept separate so a personal colour never alters client-facing branding.

nodes.label: Migration delta (current roles → target model)
nodes.rationale: Widen AccessAction/Resource unions, rewrite DEFAULT_ROLE_PERMISSIONS to five roles, migrate user.role values and backfill role_permission rows, read roles from the DB for custom roles, and enforce keys server-side.

nodes.label: TableRenderer (config-driven tables)
nodes.rationale: Every table goes through TableRenderer; a feature component is one line and all chrome comes from the theme, never inline restyling.

nodes.label: Custom table cells (cells prop escape hatch)
nodes.rationale: The cell type IS the key: unknown types resolve from the cells prop in TableCellRenderer before falling through to GenericRenderer, which knows nothing about it. Repeated looks get promoted to real GenericRenderer types.
nodes.norm_label: custom table cells (cells prop escape hatch)

nodes.label: Server-mode pagination/sort/filter query contract
nodes.rationale: Query = { ...filters, sortKey, sortDir, page, pageSize }; the API must return { data, meta: { totalCount } } and honor the params server-side.

nodes.label: Email Logo Mark (white glyph + amber dot, 63x63 PNG)
nodes.norm_label: email logo mark (white glyph + amber dot, 63x63 png)

nodes.label: HirePilotX Brand Identity (navy primary, amber #F59E0B secondary)
nodes.norm_label: hirepilotx brand identity (navy primary, amber #f59e0b secondary)
